newsitem.title: CANADA: CRICKET-FIRST INDIA-PAKISTAN ONE DAYER IN CANADA A WASHOUT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-FIRST INDIA-PAKISTAN ONE DAYER IN CANADA A WASHOUT.

text.p: Torrential rain has forced postponement of the first of five limited over matches between Pakistan and India in the unfamiliar international cricket surrounds of Toronto.

The first match of the Sahara Cup series was to be played at the Toronto Cricket, Skating and Curling Club on Saturday, but downpours on Friday flooded the ground which features one of the few turf wickets in Canada.

The opening encounter will now be staged Sunday with organisers hastily scheduling a match for Monday. The remaining matches are scheduled for next Wednesday (18th), Saturday and Sunday (21st and 22nd).
Both sides will be at full strength for the first full series of one-dayers between Pakistan and India since 1989. Political tensions make extended tours between the countries impossible.
India's 23-year-old captain Sachin Tendulkar will be under pressure to lift his side, which finished last in the recently completed three-team Singer World Series in Sri Lanka.
Wasim Akram will captain a relaxed Pakistan side, which enjoyed a Test series victory over England this summer. Akram was one of the few players yet to arrive in Toronto.

Cricket has been played since the mid 19th century in Canada but survives only as a minor sport largely through the support of the Indian, Pakistani and Caribbean communities in ethnically diverse cities like Toronto.
